disputed: Whether the AMOC has already weakened is disputed: the temperature indices (Caesar 2018, Rahmstorf 2015) and Thornalley 2018 read a decline since the 19th or mid-20th century; Terhaar 2025's heat-flux reconstruction finds none since 1963; Kilbourne et al. 2022 argue the proxies leave it uncertain. RAPID has measured it directly only since 2004.

series.label: RAPID array, 26.5°N
series.measures: overturning measured by moored instruments across the Atlantic
series.source: Moat et al. 2026, RAPID-MOCHA-WBTS array at 26N, 2004-2024 (v2024.1a), British Oceanographic Data Centre
series.note: Monthly means of the 10-day filtered, 12-hourly series.

series.label: Caesar et al. 2018
series.measures: sea-surface temperature of the subpolar gyre minus the globe's (HadISST)
series.source: Caesar et al. 2018, Nature 556, 191-196, via Caesar et al. 2021
series.note: Calibrated at 3.8 ± 0.5 Sv per K; a falling index is read as a weakening AMOC, some 3 ± 1 Sv since the mid-20th century.

series.label: Rahmstorf et al. 2015
series.measures: proxy temperature of the subpolar gyre minus the northern hemisphere's
series.source: Rahmstorf et al. 2015, Nature Climate Change 5, 475-480, via Caesar et al. 2021

series.label: Thornalley et al. 2018
series.measures: subsurface-temperature AMOC proxy from Labrador Sea and Gulf Stream cores
series.source: Thornalley et al. 2018, Nature 556, 227-230, via Caesar et al. 2021
series.note: Extended Data Fig. 4e-g of the paper; range: 2-sigma.

series.label: Terhaar et al. 2025 (ERA5)
series.measures: AMOC inferred from air-sea heat fluxes in the ERA5 reanalysis
series.source: Terhaar, Vogt & Foukal 2025, Nature Communications 16, 222, Source Data (Fig. 9a)
series.note: Decadal averages, as anomalies from 1963-2017; the spread is the standard deviation the source gives, from the fit only. Values as given, unrounded.

series.label: Terhaar et al. 2025 (JRA-55)
series.measures: AMOC inferred from air-sea heat fluxes in the JRA-55 reanalysis
series.source: Terhaar, Vogt & Foukal 2025, Nature Communications 16, 222, Source Data (Fig. 9a)
series.note: Decadal averages, as anomalies from 1963-2017; the spread is the standard deviation the source gives, from the fit only. Values as given, unrounded.
